sections.title: Encounter rules
lines: Interacting with the Monolith will reveal a battle between two Legion factions that are in stasis.
A timer will start once the Monolith is activated.
During this phase, the enemies can be "killed", breaking them out of stasis and allowing them to be fought when the timer ends for rewards.

Once the timer runs out, all the enemies that were broken out of stasis will remain and start attacking.
Killing 90% of the monsters, including all sergeants, generals, and chests, will break out all Legion monsters early.
Some Legion enemies are marked as Sergeants and have a symbol above their heads that indicate an additional reward type they will drop.
Chests and War Hoards can be damaged while in stasis and will break out nearby non-sergeants/generals when "killed".
The general of each Legion can occasionally spawn, always spawning in the far rear of the formation.
If a general spawns, the monolith will display a wave of purple on the bottom in the direction of the general.
Schism: Alternatively, taking the Timeless Conflict keystone will disable the Legion timer.
Instead, breaking out monsters and chests from stasis will contribute progress towards a Schism, as shown by a progress bar.
Once the progress bar is full, the Schism will occur and the Legion encounter will begin.
Breaking out monsters and chests with rewards or more powerful monsters will contribute more progress towards the Schism.
Generally, rarer, more rewarding spawns will spawn further away from the monolith.

sections.title: How it works
lines: Abysses spawn from Act 6 onwards and in maps.
Abysses are marked on the minimap with a green icon.
Abyss encounters spawn as multiple abyssal pits with multiple fissures branching from each.
The abyss cracks absorb the lifeforce of native monsters in the area, indicated by a green glow.
Killing monsters close to these fissures will send their souls to the abyss and close up the cracks.
Once the fissures have closed all the way to the pit, the pit will activate and spawn a large number of Abyssal monsters …
… with rarities and modifiers based on the rarities and modifiers of the slain weakened monsters.
Each Abyss encounter will spawn Abyss monsters aligned with one of the Abyssal Liches: Amanamu, Ulaman, or Kurgal.
Once most of the emerging Abyssal monsters have been killed, the pit will close up.
The pit will often spawn a chest that contains items.
Some chests will appear as a Greater version that drop more items.
Abyss encounters will always spawn at least one Greater chest.
In zone levels 78 and up, a pit may instead open an entrance to the Abyssal Depths, containing an encounter with one of two Abyssal Liches.
If an area already has an Abyss, modifiers that cause areas to contain additional Abysses will instead add two additional pits.

sections.title: Basic rules
lines: Each variety of Labyrinth requires completing a series of steps to unlock the Labyrinth for the first time.
Once these requirements have been met, that variety of Labyrinth can be run repeatedly.
Each Labyrinth contains a series of chambers connected by exits.
Three of these chambers are Aspirant's Trials, where the players will battle Izaro.
The first Trial ends when Izaro's life is reduced to 2/3 of full strength.
The second Trial starts with Izaro's life at 2/3, and ends when Izaro's life is reduced to 1/3.
The final Trial starts with Izaro's life at 1/3, and ends when Izaro is slain.
Completing all three Aspirant's Trials unlocks the Ascendancy Chamber, where the players receive their rewards for a successful Labyrinth c…
There are no waypoints or checkpoints in a Labyrinth.
Once a character leaves an active Labyrinth for any reason -- through death, logging out, exiting the game, disconnect, or crash -- the cha…
Players cannot use town portals to enter the Labyrinth; using a portal to leave the Labyrinth bars the character from returning. (When usin…
Players can access their stash immediately before each Aspirant's Trial, and in the Ascendancy Chamber.
Players can normally keep any items in their inventory and stash when they leave the Labyrinth.
Special items that can only be used in the Labyrinth -- such as keys, and items that modify the mechanics of the Aspirant's Trial -- can on…
Like quest items, these items cannot be traded or moved to a stash.
Unused special items will be dropped when the player leaves the Labyrinth for any reason.
The layout of each variant of the Labyrinth is randomly regenerated each day, at midnight (00:00) UTC.
All instances of a given Labyrinth during the day will have the same chambers arranged in the same way.
If a Labyrinth chamber contains a special element, such as a key or a Mysterious Darkshrine, then all instances of that Labyrinth that day…
This means that a given Labyrinth will be very similar if you run it multiple times on the same day; but it could be very different tomorro…

rows: Cleaver traps are typically on narrow corridor paths, attached to the side.

lines: Scarabs can drop anywhere.
